Jordan: FYI Creston's procurement team asked for an SLO summary to drop into their contract packet. They want uptime, a p99 latency number, and a sample credit calc.
Priya (Creston): Timeline is tight  review by Tue. They'd prefer p99 <= 500ms and target SLA 99.9%.
Ravi: For the packet we usually show p50/p95/p99, 30d rolling uptime, and an example credit calc (hosted baseline). I'll paste a worked example.
Jordan: Example to include: SLA=99.9%, achieved=99.6% over 30d, commitment=$30,000 -> credit = ((0.999-0.996)/0.999)*30000 ~ $90. Code snippet: ```sla=0.999
achieved=0.996
credit=(sla-achieved)/sla*commitment```
Ops-bot: Automated SLO snapshot: creston-crst-221 30d uptime=99.82%, p99=410ms. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/customers/crst-221/slo
Priya (Creston): Please add a 2-line note about failover: what we do if a region gets constrained and how that might affect latency/quality. Procurement wants transparency.
Ravi: Suggested blurb: "During capacity constraints requests may be routed to lower-cost/compatible model variants to maintain availability. This preserves uptime but can slightly increase latency or alter output characteristics; we document the fallback policy in the contract."
Jordan: Action: Ravi will update the one-pager with SLO snapshot + example calc + fallback blurb. I'll review and send to Priya by EOD Friday. Priya: ack? :thumbsup:
Priya (Creston): Ack, that works. Thanks everyone!
